To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

TNFR25 signaling induces rapid expansion of preexisting CD4(+)CD25(+)FoxP-3(+) T cells and that this expansion is dependent upon TCR, IL-2, Akt signaling and is not affected by CD80/CD86 costimulation, and that Tregs expanded by this method are suppressive and are protective against allergic lung disease in vivo.
signaling through TNFR25 selectively expands Tregs in vivo, and TNFR25-expanded CD4(+)CD25(+)FoxP(+) Tregs remain highly suppressive in vivo and are protective against allergic lung disease.

TNFR25 is constitutively expressed on Tregs in mice and that signaling through TNFR25 induces rapid and selective expansion and activation of Tregs, and that Tregs expanded and activated by TNFR25 are highly suppressive ex-vivo, and are protective in vivo against allergic lung inflammation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel mechanism for regulating Tregs in the immune system and its role in controlling allergic disease.
the development, characterization, and therapeutic use of monoclonal antibodies that target TNFR25 to expand Tregs in vivo.
the mechanisms that control the development and activity of CD4+CD25+ regulatory T cells (Tregs) and their potential use in the treatment of allergic and auto-immune disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TNFR25 is a novel target to promote Treg expansion in vivo for therapeutic use.
TNFR25 agonism is a novel approach to selectively expanding Tregs, and that Treg expansion by TNFR25 is protective in an allergic lung inflammation model.
we show that TNFRSF25 (TNFR25) is a novel regulator of Tregs that is required for their homeostatic proliferation, which is essential for maintaining the Treg pool and preventing autoimmune disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TNFR25 is a key regulator of Treg homeostasis and function.
TNF receptor super family 25 (TNF-R25) is highly expressed by Tregs.
TNFR25 is a novel Treg expansion factor and a potential therapeutic target for Treg-mediated immunotherapy.

TNFR25 is a potent inducer of Treg expansion in vivo.
